chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Isma'il ibn Jabr, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Do not eat their slaughtered meat, and do not eat in their vessels,' meaning the People of the Book.

key_terms.أَهْلَ الْكِتَابِ: The People of the Book (Jews and Christians)
key_terms.ذَبَائِحَهُمْ: Their slaughtered meat (specifically referring to animals slaughtered by non-Muslims)

ai.seo_question: What is the Shia ruling on eating the meat and using the vessels of the People of the Book?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) explicitly prohibits consuming the meat of the People of the Book and using their vessels, reflecting the dominant Shia view of *ghul* (impurity) in their tableware. This ruling distinguishes between the permissibility of their meat under specific conditions and the stricter prohibition regarding their utensils, which are often used for non-halal sacrifices or wine. The narration underscores the practical application of ritual purity (*taharah*) in daily interactions with non-Muslims.
